run_metadata.seed_myth:
# The First Star

In the time before time, when the world was young and formless, there lived a weaver named Celestia who worked in absolute darkness. She wove the fabric of the sky each night, but her tapestries were empty and black, for light had not yet been born.

One evening, Celestia pricked her finger on her silver needle. A single drop of her blood fell onto the dark canvas above. Instead of disappearing, it began to glow—first dimly, then brilliantly—transforming into a point of radiant light. Celestia gasped in wonder.

"What are you?" she whispered.

"I am a star," the light replied, "born from your dedication and sacrifice. Where there is passion and pain, there shall be illumination."

Inspired, Celestia continued her work with renewed purpose. Each night, she would prick her finger deliberately, and each drop became a new star. She scattered them across her tapestry in patterns that told stories—a hunter, a bear, a great river flowing through the heavens.

When her mortal days ended, the gods transformed Celestia herself into the brightest star of all, so she could forever watch over her celestial creation. And that is why, even now, the stars shine brightest on the darkest nights.
